::: {.book-summary} ## Book Summary Insight Judges describes Israel's repeated cycle of sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance. The book demonstrates humanity's need for a righteous King who can faithfully lead God's people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 1
Judges 1:2
Judah shall go up
### Why This Verse Beginning of conquest after Joshua ### Chapter Insight This chapter describes Israel's incomplete conquest of Canaan. The key verse highlights the consequences of failing to fully obey God's commands. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 2
Judges 2:10
Another generation knew not the LORD
### Why This Verse Key theme of Judges ### Chapter Insight This chapter explains Israel's recurring cycle of sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance. The key verse summarizes the spiritual decline that defines the book. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 3
Judges 3:9
The LORD raised up a deliverer
### Why This Verse Introduces the judge cycle ### Chapter Insight This chapter introduces the first judges raised up by God. The key verse emphasizes God's mercy in providing deliverers for His people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 4
Judges 4:9
The honor shall not be yours
### Why This Verse Deborah's prophecy to Barak ### Chapter Insight This chapter records Deborah and Barak's victory over Sisera. The key verse highlights God's power working through faithful leaders. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 5
Judges 5:31
Let them that love Him be as the sun
### Why This Verse Conclusion of Deborah's song ### Chapter Insight This chapter celebrates victory through the Song of Deborah. The key verse praises God for delivering Israel through willing servants. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 6
Judges 6:12
The LORD is with thee, mighty man of valor
### Why This Verse Gideon's famous call ### Chapter Insight This chapter recounts Gideon's call to deliver Israel. The key verse emphasizes God's presence rather than human strength. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 7
Judges 7:2
Lest Israel boast
### Why This Verse God's purpose in reducing the army ### Chapter Insight This chapter records Gideon's victory with a reduced army. The key verse demonstrates that salvation belongs to the Lord alone. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 8
Judges 8:23
The LORD shall rule over you
### Why This Verse Gideon's refusal of kingship ### Chapter Insight This chapter concludes Gideon's leadership and reveals Israel's continuing spiritual weakness. The key verse warns against forgetting God's deliverance. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 9
Judges 9:8
The trees went forth to anoint a king
### Why This Verse Jotham's famous parable ### Chapter Insight This chapter records Abimelech's violent pursuit of power. The key verse illustrates the destructive consequences of selfish ambition. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 10
Judges 10:16
His soul was grieved for Israel
### Why This Verse God's compassion despite rebellion ### Chapter Insight This chapter describes Israel's renewed rebellion and suffering. The key verse reveals God's grief over His people's persistent unfaithfulness. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 11
Judges 11:30
Jephthah made a vow
### Why This Verse Beginning of the tragic vow account ### Chapter Insight This chapter recounts Jephthah's rise and tragic vow. The key verse emphasizes faith in God's deliverance while warning against rash commitments. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 12
Judges 12:6
Shibboleth
### Why This Verse Famous origin of the term ### Chapter Insight This chapter records conflict among the tribes and the ministry of additional judges. The key verse highlights the divisions resulting from pride and rivalry. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 13
Judges 13:5
He shall begin to deliver Israel
### Why This Verse Samson's birth announcement ### Chapter Insight This chapter announces the birth of Samson. The key verse reveals God's sovereign preparation of a deliverer. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 14
Judges 14:14
Out of the eater came forth meat
### Why This Verse Samson's riddle ### Chapter Insight This chapter begins Samson's public ministry. The key verse demonstrates God's ability to accomplish His purposes through imperfect people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 15
Judges 15:16
With the jawbone of a donkey
### Why This Verse Samson's victory song ### Chapter Insight This chapter records Samson's conflicts with the Philistines. The key verse highlights God's empowering strength in battle. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 16
Judges 16:28
O Lord GOD, remember me
### Why This Verse Samson's final prayer ### Chapter Insight This chapter recounts Samson's downfall and final victory. The key verse demonstrates that God's grace can still work through repentance. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 17
Judges 17:6
Every man did what was right in his own eyes
### Why This Verse One of Judges' defining verses ### Chapter Insight This chapter introduces Micah's idolatry. The key verse reveals the spiritual confusion caused by abandoning God's standards. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 18
Judges 18:1
In those days there was no king in Israel
### Why This Verse Sets context for tribal disorder ### Chapter Insight This chapter records the tribe of Dan's migration and idolatry. The key verse illustrates the consequences of self-directed religion. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 19
Judges 19:30
Consider it, take counsel, and speak
### Why This Verse Response to national outrage ### Chapter Insight This chapter recounts one of Israel's darkest moral failures. The key verse demonstrates the depth of national spiritual decay. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 20
Judges 20:18
They inquired of God
### Why This Verse Beginning of civil war account ### Chapter Insight This chapter records civil war against Benjamin. The key verse highlights the devastating consequences of unchecked sin. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 21
Judges 21:25
Every man did what was right in his own eyes
### Why This Verse Closing summary of the book ### Chapter Insight This chapter concludes with efforts to preserve Benjamin. The key verse summarizes the book's theme of moral chaos without godly leadership. :::
